description: Reference render corpus for the Pertylizer Sound Core V2 migration (plans/v2, task P00A-T001). Each case names a V1 project, the exact settings that render it, and what V2 must preserve or is intended to change. Regenerate the fixture projects and refresh the digests with `cargo run -p pertylizer --bin gen_corpus`.

cases.title: Basic subtractive voice
cases.purpose: The minimal render path: one oscillator through one static low-pass into an envelope-gated amplifier, played as four separated notes so each note-on is an isolated onset and each note-off an isolated release.

preserve.behavior: Each of the four notes sounds at the pitch the pattern declares, with the same fundamental frequency V1 produces.
The amplitude envelope's attack, decay, sustain and release landmarks stay within measurement tolerance of V1's.
The static low-pass leaves the same spectral balance: per-band energy tracks V1's across the whole render.

change.behavior: Note onsets land on the exact sample the tick maps to, not on the first sample of the render block containing it.
change.rationale: V1 dispatches sequencer events on block boundaries, so an onset can sit up to one block late and the error depends on the block size. Sample-accurate scheduling is the Phase 3 objective and is one of the corrections the master plan's audio comparison policy names.

cases.title: Polyphonic pad with voice stealing
cases.purpose: Eight overlapping sustained notes against a four-voice instrument, so the allocator has to steal four times inside the rendered window and the release tail of each stolen voice is cut short.

preserve.behavior: At most four voices sound at any instant: the instrument's voice ceiling is never exceeded. Fewer sound during the opening, while the notes are still entering one by one.
Which note is stolen is a function of the arrangement alone, so two renders of this project choose the same victims in the same order.

The overall RMS envelope tracks V1's through each steal. This is a claim about matching V1, not about the transition being smooth: V1 resets a stolen voice, so its own envelope steps, and a V2 that removed the step would be changing behaviour rather than preserving it.

cases.title: Mod Matrix routed filter sweep
cases.purpose: One Mod Matrix slot carrying an LFO to the filter cutoff, with no patch cable to the cutoff CV port, so the sweep can only come through the matrix path.

preserve.behavior: The cutoff sweeps at the LFO's rate and over the depth the slot amount sets; the spectral centroid oscillates with the same period and excursion V1 produces.
A voice's LFO phase is zeroed when the allocator hands the voice out, so both notes in the render begin their sweep from the same phase.

change.behavior: Modulation is evaluated at a declared control rate rather than once per render block, so the sweep's step size no longer depends on the block size the host or the offline renderer happens to use.
change.rationale: A fixed control rate is one of the corrections the master plan's audio comparison policy names, and ADR-0001 makes the internal render quantum independent of the host block — modulation tied to the block would reintroduce exactly the dependency that decision removes.

cases.title: Send into a reverb return, with a master compressor
cases.purpose: Three paths the voice cases never touch: a post-fader track send, a return bus running its own fully-wet effect chain, and a master chain applied to the summed mix. Short repeated notes make the send's contribution and the compressor's recovery separately visible.

preserve.behavior: The dry track and the return both reach the master: muting the return alone changes the render, and so does zeroing the send.
The reverb tail continues past the last note for the same duration and decays on the same curve.
The master compressor engages on the same transients and recovers over the same interval, so the peak-to-RMS ratio of the render tracks V1's.

change.behavior: Bus summing and the master chain run with linear headroom rather than clamping intermediate stages, so a mix that exceeded full scale internally comes back with its shape intact.
change.rationale: Linear headroom is one of the corrections the master plan's audio comparison policy names. Where V1 clamped inside the chain, V2 will differ audibly on exactly the material this case renders, and that difference is the point rather than a regression.

cases.title: Instrument insert chain: distortion into delay
cases.purpose: An insert chain inside the instrument, between voice summing and the mixer, which is a position no other case exercises: CORPUS-0004's effects sit on a return bus and on the master and only ever see a signal that has already left the instrument. A held fifth makes that position measurable, and one isolated short note near the end leaves the delay ringing into silence. The oscillator's note-on phase randomization is turned off (uni_phase 0, against a shipped default of 1.0) so that the render depends on the insert chain rather than on which voice the allocator handed each note.

preserve.behavior: The chain processes the summed voices, not each voice. Rendering the dyad through the chain differs from summing two single-note renders of the same chain: with only the soft clipper in the chain the difference has an RMS 3.1 dB below the case's own, against a null control - the same construction with an empty chain - at -147 dB relative, which is floating-point rounding. A V2 that moved insert effects into the voice graph would still sound plausible on a single note and would fail here.

Chain state is shared across voices rather than owned by one. With only the delay in the chain, the dyad rendered whole still differs from the two single renders summed, by 35 dB below the case's own RMS and 112 dB above the null control. Two notes can only interact inside a delay whose line they share, through the soft clip on its feedback write; per-voice delay lines would land at the control.

Chain state outlives the notes that produced it. The delay's repeats fill the gap between the dyad and the isolated note, when every voice has already been released, and continue 2.3 s past the final note-off: measured on V1 the tail runs from -14.8 dBFS at 1.2 s to -70.7 dBFS at 3.4 s, against a control with both inserts removed that is digital silence from 1.7 s on.

The chain runs in the order patch.settings.effect_chain_order declares. Rendering the same two modules in the opposite order is a different signal - clean repeats of a clipped dyad rather than a clipped sum of repeats - and measured on V1 the reversal moves the render's RMS by 5.97 dB. The field is authored data rather than a display hint.

change.behavior: An insert whose module is absent from the chain order is refused at compilation rather than appended to the end with a warning.
change.rationale: V1 recovers from an incomplete effect_chain_order by appending the unnamed modules, so the rendered order is partly V1's choice rather than the project's. Under ADR-0021 part 2 admission may refuse a plan but may never silently change authored topology to make it fit, and an appended insert is exactly that. This case authors a complete order, so the correction changes nothing here - it is recorded because this is the case that would otherwise be used to justify the fallback.

cases.title: Keyboard-panned stereo voice
cases.purpose: One mono oscillator passes through the Keyboard Panner while three separated notes fall below, at, and above its center note. No other stereo mechanism is present, so the channel-energy movement belongs to the panner.

preserve.behavior: The low note has more energy in the left channel, the center note has equal channel energy, and the high note has more energy in the right channel.
Changing note pitch changes only the panner position and oscillator frequency; it does not collapse or exchange the two output channels.

cases.title: YAMS control-rate amplifier
cases.purpose: A one-line Script program writes a constant to the amplifier's only CV input. The oscillator is audible only if the program is installed, evaluated, and routed through out1.

preserve.behavior: The Script program out1 = 0.65 opens the amplifier to the same constant gain V1 produces for the held note.
The installed program and its out1-to-CV routing survive project loading and offline rendering; the result is audible rather than the silent no-program control.

cases.title: YAMS audio-rate stereo transform
cases.purpose: A two-line AudioScript applies +0.75 gain to the left copy and -0.5 gain to the right copy of one sine oscillator. With no state, randomness, or stock effect, every sample tests audio-rate program execution and stereo wiring directly.

preserve.behavior: The AudioScript runs once per sample and preserves the source waveform while applying the authored signed gains: left is 0.75 times the input and right is -0.5 times the input.
The installed audio-rate program and both stereo cables survive project loading and offline rendering; neither output silently falls back to zero or mono.

cases.title: Tempo ramp and step arrangement
cases.purpose: Six short notes at equal tick intervals cross a 90-to-180 BPM ramp and a later step to 120 BPM. Their unequal sample intervals prove that the renderer consumed the authored tempo map rather than one constant tempo.

preserve.behavior: The authored tempo changes affect note spacing: equal tick intervals render at unequal sample intervals through the ramp and change again after the 120 BPM step.
Note order, pitch, and the association between each onset and its musical tick are preserved across the tempo changes.

change.behavior: The exact sample positions inside a tempo ramp remain unsupported until Phase 3 accepts one ramp-position law.
change.rationale: Phase 0A can capture V1's observable output without making the Phase 3 decision. The comparison must report this law as unsupported scope instead of silently treating either V1 parity or a changed position as correct.

cases.title: Two tracks sharing one instrument
cases.purpose: Two patterns on independent tracks address the same persisted instrument id with the same note at the same time, at unity and half track gain. A deterministic subtractive patch keeps the observation about sharing rather than script-seed identity.

preserve.behavior: Two tracks may reference one InstrumentId and their simultaneous note streams both render through that shared instrument rather than one track replacing the other.
Each track's gain remains attached to its own voices when both tracks use the same instrument; the half-gain second track does not reduce the unity-gain first track.

planned.why_absent: A sampler case needs a sample asset, so a plain project cannot reproduce it by itself; the project and asset must travel as one deterministic bundle before this category can be rendered headlessly.
